```{r}
# 1. Access the final proportion matrix (weights_full)
myRCTD <- readRDS("/home/mattia/Thesis/03Slide4/Random data/myRCTD_spatial_bins_results.rds")
proportion_matrix <- myRCTD@assays@data@listData[["weights_full"]]

# 2. Transpose the matrix to have Pixels (Barcodes) as ROWS, which is required for easy filtering
proportion_df <- as.data.frame(t(proportion_matrix))

# Sanity Check: Print the first few columns to confirm cell type names are correct
colnames(proportion_df)
```

```{r}
cell_type_to_remove <- "unk" 

# Define the minimum proportion threshold for removal (e.g., 1%)
# Spots with this cell type >= this proportion will be REMOVED.
threshold <- 0.05 

# 3. Create a logical vector to identify spots to keep:
# We keep spots where the proportion of the unwanted cell type is strictly BELOW the threshold.
spots_to_keep <- proportion_df[[cell_type_to_remove]] < threshold

# 4. Get the list of barcodes (pixel IDs) to keep
barcodes_to_keep <- rownames(proportion_df)[spots_to_keep]

# Optional: Report the impact of the filter
num_removed <- sum(!spots_to_keep)
num_total <- length(spots_to_keep)
print(paste0("Total spots to remove: ", num_removed, " (", round(num_removed/num_total*100, 2), "%)"))
```

```{r}
# 5. Subset the SpatialExperiment object
spatial_experiment <- readRDS("/home/mattia/Thesis/03Slide4/Random data/spatial_experiment.rds")
spe_filtered <- spatial_experiment[, barcodes_to_keep]

# Final Check: Print the new number of spots
print(paste0("New number of spatial spots (columns): ", ncol(spe_filtered)))
```

```{r}
# 1. Get the spatial coordinates (colData or from spatialCoords)
coords_original <- as.data.frame(spatialCoords(spatial_experiment))
coords_filtered <- as.data.frame(spatialCoords(spe_filtered))

# 2. Add a status column to each data frame
coords_original$Status <- "Original (All Spots)"
coords_filtered$Status <- "Filtered (Kept Spots Only)"

# 3. Rename columns for generic use (x-y coordinates)
colnames(coords_original)[1:2] <- c("x_coord", "y_coord")
colnames(coords_filtered)[1:2] <- c("x_coord", "y_coord")

# 4. Combine the data frames for a single ggplot call
plot_data <- rbind(coords_original, coords_filtered)
```

```{r}
plot_filtered_effect <- ggplot(plot_data, aes(x = x_coord, y = y_coord, color = Status)) +
  geom_point(size = 0.5) + # Adjust size based on your data density
  facet_wrap(~Status) +
  scale_y_reverse() + # Standard spatial plots often reverse the Y-axis
  labs(
    title = paste("Spatial Spot Removal (Threshold:", threshold * 100, "% of", cell_type_to_remove, "removed)"),
    x = "Spatial X Coordinate",
    y = "Spatial Y Coordinate"
  ) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold"),
    strip.text = element_text(size = 12)
  )

print(plot_filtered_effect)
```

```{r}
# Define the list of all 14 cell type proportion columns
#CELL_TYPE_COLS <- c("AstC-EE", "aEC", "classIII-EE", "Copper", "daEC", "dEC", #"EB", "EEP", "ISC", "LFC", "mEC", "MT", "pEC", "Tk-EE")

CELL_TYPE_COLS <- c("EE", "aEC", "Copper", "daEC", "dEC", "EB", "ISC", "LFC", "mEC", "MT", "pEC")

# 1. Filter the original proportion data for only the kept spots (barcodes_to_keep)
# Assuming proportion_df is a data.frame or matrix
proportion_df_filtered <- proportion_df[barcodes_to_keep, ] 

# 2. Loop through each cell type and add the column to spe_filtered
for (ct_name in CELL_TYPE_COLS) {
    
    # Check if the column exists in the proportion data
    if (ct_name %in% colnames(proportion_df_filtered)) {
        
        # Extract the single column (as a vector) from the filtered proportions
        cell_type_proportions <- proportion_df_filtered[[ct_name]]
        
        # Add this vector as a new column to the colData of the SpatialExperiment object
        colData(spe_filtered)[[ct_name]] <- cell_type_proportions
        
        # Optional check:
        print(paste("Successfully added:", ct_name))
        
    } else {
        warning(paste("Column not found in proportion_df_filtered:", ct_name))
    }
}

# Optional: Ensure the barcode names match (though not strictly necessary if order is preserved)
rownames(colData(spe_filtered)) <- colnames(spe_filtered)
```

```{r}
# --- 1. Identify the Cell Type with the Highest Proportion for each Pixel ---
CELL_TYPE_COLS <- c("EE", "aEC", "Copper", "daEC", "dEC", "EB", "ISC", "LFC", "mEC", "MT", "pEC")

# Define the list of all 14 cell type proportion columns
#CELL_TYPE_COLS <- c("AstC.EE", "aEC", "classIII.EE", "Copper", "daEC", "dEC", #"EB", "EEP", "ISC", "LFC", "mEC", "MT", "pEC", "Tk.EE")

# Extract the colData (metadata) from your SpatialExperiment object
colData_df <- as.data.frame(colData(spe_filtered))

# Create a new column 'Most_Likely_CellType'
# The apply function finds the column name (cell type) that corresponds to the maximum value in each row (pixel)
colData_df$Most_Likely_CellType <- apply(
    colData_df[, CELL_TYPE_COLS], # Look only at the cell type proportion columns
    1,                            # Apply function across rows (pixels)
    function(x) CELL_TYPE_COLS[which.max(x)] # Find the index of the max value and return the cell type name
)

# Add the new column back to the colData of your SpatialExperiment object
colData(spe_filtered)$Most_Likely_CellType <- colData_df$Most_Likely_CellType


# --- 2. Prepare Data and Plot the Most Likely Cell Type ---

# Prepare data frame: Combine colData and spatialCoords from the FILTERED object
plot_data_ML <- data.frame(
    colData(spe_filtered),
    spatialCoords(spe_filtered)
)
colnames(plot_data_ML)[grep("coord", colnames(plot_data_ML))] <- c("x", "y")

# Get a color palette with enough distinct colors for all 14 cell types
# The 'Set3' palette from RColorBrewer is a good option for categorical data up to 12 colors.
# Since you have 14, you might need a custom or mixed palette.
celltype_colors <- colorRampPalette(brewer.pal(n = 12, name = "Set3"))(length(CELL_TYPE_COLS))


# Generate the ggplot visualization
most_likely_plot <- ggplot(
    plot_data_ML,
    aes(x = x, y = y, color = Most_Likely_CellType)
) +
    geom_point(size = 1.5) +
    scale_color_manual(
        values = celltype_colors, # Use the custom color palette
        name = "Most Likely Cell Type"
    ) +
    scale_y_reverse() + # Reverse Y-axis to match image orientation
    coord_fixed() + # Ensures the spatial aspect ratio is correct
    theme_void() + # Removes axes and background
    ggtitle("Spatial Mapping of Most Likely Cell Type (RTCD)") +
    theme(
        plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold"),
        legend.position = "right"
    )

print(most_likely_plot)
```

```{r}
# --- 1. Prepare Data for Faceting ---

# Use the same base plot_data_ML dataframe from the previous step

# Transform the data from "wide" format (14 columns) to "long" format (3 columns: x, y, CellType, Proportion)
# This is necessary for ggplot's facet_wrap
plot_data_long <- plot_data_ML %>%
    pivot_longer(
        cols = all_of(CELL_TYPE_COLS), # Columns to gather
        names_to = "CellType",         # New column for the cell type names
        values_to = "Proportion"       # New column for the proportion values
    )

# --- 2. Generate the Faceted ggplot Visualization ---

faceted_proportion_plot <- ggplot(
    plot_data_long,
    aes(x = x, y = y, color = Proportion)
) +
    geom_point(size = 1.5) +
    scale_color_viridis_c(name = "Proportion", option = "magma") + # Continuous color scale
    scale_y_reverse() +
    coord_fixed() +
    theme_void() +
    # This creates a separate plot for each cell type
    facet_wrap(~ CellType, ncol = 4) + # Adjust ncol for desired layout
    ggtitle("Spatial Proportion Map of All Cell Types (RTCD)") +
    theme(
        plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold"),
        strip.text = element_text(size = 8, face = "bold") # Format the cell type titles
    )

print(faceted_proportion_plot)
```

```{r}
# 1. Prepare Data outside of Shiny
coords_data <- as.data.frame(spatialCoords(spe_filtered))
colnames(coords_data) <- c("x", "y")
coords_data$barcode <- colnames(spe_filtered)
coords_data$id <- 1:nrow(coords_data)

# 2. Define the Shiny App (UI and Server logic)
ui <- fluidPage(
  titlePanel("Manual Gut Selection (Plotly Lasso Draw)"),
  sidebarLayout(
    sidebarPanel(
      actionButton("save_gut_1", "Save Gut 1 Selection"),
      actionButton("save_gut_2", "Save Gut 2 Selection"),
      actionButton("save_gut_3", "Save Gut 3 Selection"),
      hr(),
      actionButton("done_button", "DONE: Close App & Save Data"),
      hr(),
      p("Instructions: **Look for the toolbar in the plot's top-right corner.** Click the Lasso tool icon (a free-form loop) to select points. Draw a shape around a gut section, then click the corresponding 'Save Gut X' button."),
      p("Click the 'DONE' button when all three guts are saved.")
    ),
    mainPanel(
      plotlyOutput("spatial_plot")
    )
  )
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  
  selected_barcodes <- reactiveValues(gut_1 = character(0), gut_2 = character(0), gut_3 = character(0))
  
  # Render the main plot using Plotly
  output$spatial_plot <- renderPlotly({
    plot_ly(
      coords_data, 
      x = ~x, 
      y = ~y, 
      type = 'scatter', 
      mode = 'markers',
      marker = list(size = 5, color = 'blue', opacity = 0.5),
      source = "A" # Source ID for event capture
    ) %>%
      layout(
        title = "Use Lasso Tool to Select Points",
        yaxis = list(autorange = "reversed")
      ) 
  })
  
  get_selected_points <- reactive({
    event_data("plotly_selected", source = "A")
  })
  
  observeEvent(input$save_gut_1, {
    selected <- get_selected_points()
    req(selected)
    selected_indices <- selected$pointNumber + 1
    selected_barcodes$gut_1 <- coords_data$barcode[selected_indices]
    cat(paste("Gut 1 saved with", length(selected_barcodes$gut_1), "spots.\n"))
  })
  
  observeEvent(input$save_gut_2, {
    selected <- get_selected_points()
    req(selected)
    selected_indices <- selected$pointNumber + 1
    selected_barcodes$gut_2 <- coords_data$barcode[selected_indices]
    cat(paste("Gut 2 saved with", length(selected_barcodes$gut_2), "spots.\n"))
  })
  
  observeEvent(input$save_gut_3, {
    selected <- get_selected_points()
    req(selected)
    selected_indices <- selected$pointNumber + 1
    selected_barcodes$gut_3 <- coords_data$barcode[selected_indices]
    cat(paste("Gut 3 saved with", length(selected_barcodes$gut_3), "spots.\n"))
  })
  
  observeEvent(input$done_button, {
    stopApp(list(
      barcodes_gut_1 = selected_barcodes$gut_1,
      barcodes_gut_2 = selected_barcodes$gut_2,
      barcodes_gut_3 = selected_barcodes$gut_3
    ))
  })
} 

# Run the app and save the results
selection_results <- runApp(list(ui = ui, server = server), launch.browser = TRUE)
```

```{r}
# --- Custom Conversion Function (Final Version) ---
create_monocle_cds_spatial <- function(spe_obj) {
    library(monocle3)
    library(SingleCellExperiment) 
    
    expr_matrix <- counts(spe_obj)
    cell_data <- as.data.frame(colData(spe_obj))
    feature_data <- as.data.frame(rowData(spe_obj))
    
    # Ensure gene_short_name exists to prevent warnings/errors
    if (!"gene_short_name" %in% colnames(feature_data)) {
        feature_data$gene_short_name <- rownames(feature_data) 
    }
    
    cds <- new_cell_data_set(
        expression_data = expr_matrix,
        cell_metadata = cell_data,
        gene_metadata = feature_data
    )
    
    # CRITICAL FIX: Set the spatial coordinates as the UMAP dimension.
    spatial_coords <- spatialCoords(spe_obj)
    colnames(spatial_coords) <- c("x", "y")
    reducedDims(cds)$UMAP <- spatial_coords 
    
    return(cds)
}
```

```{r}
print("--- Starting Spatial Trajectory Learning for spe_gut_1 ---")

# --- A. Conversion and Trajectory Setup for Gut 1 ---
cds_gut_1 <- create_monocle_cds_spatial(spe_gut_1) 
    
# --- B. Spatial Trajectory Learning ---

# 1. Learn Graph from Spatial Data (UMAP)
# This step still fails because of the internal cluster check.
# cds_gut_1 <- learn_graph(cds_gut_1) 

# Run cluster_cells, forcing it to use the spatial UMAP
# This satisfies the internal check and uses the spatial data as the basis.
cds_gut_1 <- cluster_cells(cds_gut_1)
cds_gut_1@clusters$UMAP$partitions[] <- factor("1")   # Merge partitions to bridge gap

# Now, learn_graph will see the necessary cluster slots and use the spatial UMAP.
cds_gut_1 <- learn_graph(cds_gut_1, use_partition = FALSE) 

print("Spatial trajectory graph learned. Now ordering cells...")

# --- C. Order Cells and Calculate Pseudotime ---
spatial_coords <- spatialCoords(spe_gut_1)

# Identify the root node (leftmost spot for horizontal trajectory)
root_node_barcodes <- head(
    colnames(cds_gut_1)[order(spatial_coords[, 1])], 
    n = 1
)

# Order the cells based on the chosen root
cds_gut_1 <- order_cells(cds_gut_1, root_cells = root_node_barcodes)

# --- D. Extract and Scale Scores ---
current_scores <- pseudotime(cds_gut_1)
min_pt <- min(current_scores, na.rm = TRUE)
max_pt <- max(current_scores, na.rm = TRUE)
scaled_scores <- (current_scores - min_pt) / (max_pt - min_pt) * 100

# --- E. Store Result Back in SpatialExperiment object ---
colData(spe_gut_1)$spe_gut_1_Pseudotime_Score <- scaled_scores

print("✅ Spatial-based Pseudotime scores calculated and saved to spe_gut_1.")
```

```{r}
# Define the complete list of 11 cell type fraction columns (matching previous definition)
CELL_TYPE_COLS_FINAL <- c("EE", "aEC", "Copper", "daEC", "dEC", "EB", "ISC", "LFC", "mEC", "MT", "pEC")

# --- Function to Prepare Data for One Gut ---
prepare_gut_data <- function(spe_obj, gut_id) {
    # Determine the correct pseudotime column name for this object
    pt_col_name <- paste0("spe_gut_", substring(gut_id, 5), "_Pseudotime_Score")
    
    # Identify which columns actually exist in the object's colData
    existing_cols <- colnames(colData(spe_obj))
    available_ct_cols <- intersect(CELL_TYPE_COLS_FINAL, existing_cols)
    
    # Verify pt_col_name exists
    if (!pt_col_name %in% existing_cols) {
        stop(paste("Pseudotime column", pt_col_name, "not found in object."))
    }
    
    # Extract Pseudotime and available cell type columns
    data_cols <- as.data.frame(colData(spe_obj))[, c(pt_col_name, available_ct_cols)]
    
    # Rename Pseudotime column consistently
    data_cols$Pseudotime <- data_cols[[pt_col_name]]
    data_cols$GutID <- gut_id
    
    # Keep only Pseudotime, GutID, and the cell type columns
    data_cols <- data_cols[, c("Pseudotime", "GutID", available_ct_cols)]
    
    return(data_cols)
}

# Combine data from all three guts
df_1_wide <- prepare_gut_data(spe_gut_1, "Gut 1")
df_2_wide <- prepare_gut_data(spe_gut_2, "Gut 2")
df_3_wide <- prepare_gut_data(spe_gut_3, "Gut 3")

combined_wide_df <- rbind(df_1_wide, df_2_wide, df_3_wide)

# 2. Pivot Data to Long Format (Melt)
# Identify which cell type columns are actually present in the combined data
available_ct_cols_for_pivot <- intersect(CELL_TYPE_COLS_FINAL, colnames(combined_wide_df))

combined_long_df <- combined_wide_df %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = all_of(available_ct_cols_for_pivot),
    names_to = "CellType",
    values_to = "Fraction"
  )

# Clean up cell type names for plotting (replace dots/hyphens with spaces)
combined_long_df$CellType_Clean <- gsub("[\\.-]", " ", combined_long_df$CellType)
```

```{r}
# 3. Generate Faceted Visualization

 geom_point(aes(color = GutID), alpha = 0.6, size = 1.5) +
# Use a trend line that is more responsive to local variation
 geom_smooth(method = "loess", span = 0.2, color = "black", linetype = "solid", se = FALSE, linewidth = 0.5) + 
 scale_color_manual(
 values = c("Gut 1" = "#E69F00", "Gut 2" = "#56B4E9", "Gut 3" = "#009E73"),
 name = "Gut Section"
 ) +
 # Create a separate panel for each cell type
 facet_wrap(~ CellType_Clean, scales = "free_y", ncol = 4) + 
 theme_bw(base_size = 12) +
 labs(
 title = "Cell Type Fraction Distribution Along Spatial Axis",
 x = "Pseudotime (Spatial Position)",
 y = "Cell Type Fraction (% of Total Cells)"
 ) +
 theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5))

print(final_plot_responsive)
```

```{r}
# --- 1. Prepare Colors (RColorBrewer) ---
# Since we have 14 cell types, we need a palette large enough.
# We will use a colorRampPalette based on a diverse palette like 'Set3' or 'Paired' 
# and interpolate to get exactly 14 colors.

num_celltypes <- length(unique(combined_long_df$CellType_Clean))
# Use 'Set3' as a base, which is good for categorical data, and expand it to 14 colors
custom_colors <- colorRampPalette(brewer.pal(n = 12, name = "Set3"))(num_celltypes)


# --- 2. Generate the Combined LOESS Plot with Facets ---

combined_celltype_faceted_plot <- ggplot(
    combined_long_df,
    aes(
        x = Pseudotime,
        y = Fraction,
        # Map color to the cell type
        color = CellType_Clean,
        # Group by CellType_Clean ensures separate LOESS curves are calculated
        group = CellType_Clean
    )
) +
    # Use geom_smooth with method="loess" for the smooth curve
    geom_smooth(
        method = "loess",
        span = 0.2,
        se = FALSE, # Hide confidence intervals
        linewidth = 1.5
    ) +

    # Set the colors using the RColorBrewer-derived custom palette
    scale_color_manual(
        values = custom_colors,
        name = "Cell Type"
    ) +

    # --- Implement Facet Wrap by GutID (as requested) ---
    facet_wrap(
        ~ GutID,
        scales = "free_y", # Allows y-axis to adjust for each gut's data range
        ncol = 3           # Arrange in a single row
    ) +

    labs(
        title = "Cell Type Trajectories Across Individual Gut Sections",
        subtitle = "LOESS Proportion vs. Pseudotime for all Cell Types",
        x = "Pseudotime (Spatial Position along Gut Axis)",
        y = "Deconvolved Cell Type Fraction"
    ) +
    theme_bw(base_size = 14) +
    theme(
        plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold"),
        plot.subtitle = element_text(hjust = 0.5),
        # Ensure the background strips of the facets are visible
        strip.background = element_rect(fill = "gray90", color = NA),
        strip.text = element_text(face = "bold")
    )

print(combined_celltype_faceted_plot)
```

```{r}
    aes(

        # Group by CellType_Clean ensures separate LOESS curves are calculated
        group = CellType_Clean
    )
) +
    # Use geom_smooth with method="loess" for the smooth curve
    geom_smooth(
        method = "loess",
        span = 0.2,
        se = FALSE, # Hide confidence intervals
        linewidth = 1.5
    ) +

    # Set the colors using the RColorBrewer-derived custom palette
```
